sec: RANK/RANKL/OPG, calcitonin and the bone cycle · p867

items.q: On the osteoblast surface, PTH and vitamin D upregulate RANKL, which binds ___ on pre-osteoclasts (with M-CSF) to activate osteoclasts.
items.exp: RANKL (from osteoblasts) binds RANK on preosteoclasts with M-CSF → active osteoclast (acid secretion, lysosome, ruffled membrane). (Book p867)

opts: Physiological inhibition of the RANK–RANKL interaction
items.exp: OPG physiologically inhibits RANK–RANKL interaction. (Book p867)

items.q: Calcitonin binds receptors on the basal surface of osteoclasts to:
items.exp: Calcitonin inhibits osteoclast → inhibits bone resorption. (Book p867)

items.q: Calcitonin is used to treat hypercalcaemia because it also:
items.exp: It stimulates renal calcium clearance causing hypocalcaemia, hence used in hypercalcaemia. (Book p867)

items.q: Match the bone cycle steps to duration — 1) Osteoclast activation + bone resorption  2) Reversal + bone formation + mineralisation … A) 3 months  B) 3 weeks
items.exp: Resorption phase (steps 1–2) ~3 weeks; reversal/formation/mineralisation (3–5) ~3 months. (Book p867)

items.q: The correct order of the bone remodelling cycle is:
opts: Osteoclast activation → resorption → reversal → formation → mineralisation
items.exp: Steps: 1 osteoclast activation, 2 bone resorption, 3 reversal, 4 bone formation, 5 mineralisation. (Book p867)
